Name: Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Water | Land Use & Agriculture
Scope_And_Commitments:
Overarching statutory plan for improving England's natural environment. Sets out approach to meeting all Environment Act 2021 targets (species abundance, habitat, water, air, waste, soil). Updated Dec 2025. Covers 10 goals. Includes interim targets and monitoring through Environmental Indicator Framework (EIF). Applies across government with departments sharing delivery responsibility.

[VERSION HISTORY] EIP 2025 (Dec 2025) is the second statutory plan under Environment Act 2021 s.9 (replacing EIP 2023, Jan 2023). Sets out approach to meeting all Environment Act 2021 targets across 10 goals. 66 EIF indicators monitor progress. EIP must be reviewed at least every 5 years. Applies across government. Previous version: EIP 2023 published January 2023. [Themes: nature-based solutions; natural capital; ecosystem services]

Name: National Adaptation Programme (NAP3) 2023–2028
Policy_Sector: Climate | Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture | Governance, Society & Data

Government's statutory strategy for preparing England for climate change impacts. Actions from all departments. CCC assesses annually and published critical 2025 progress report.

Name: UK Net Zero Strategy / Carbon Budget Delivery Plan (CBDP) 2023
Policy_Sector: Climate | Energy | Land Use & Agriculture | Finance
Scope_And_Commitments:
Policy plan setting out government's approach to meeting CB4–CB6 carbon budgets and 2050 net-zero target. Covers 9 sectors: electricity, buildings, transport, industry, agriculture/land, aviation, shipping, waste/F-gases, fuel supply. Contains sectoral pathways, policies and targets including ZEV mandate, heat pump installation targets, offshore wind ambition. Subject to ongoing JR scrutiny.

Intl_Links: [INT-L-003] Paris Agreement; [INT-P-010] Glasgow Leaders' Declaration on Forests and Land Use (COP26, 2021)

Name: Clean Power 2030 Action Plan
Policy_Sector: Climate | Energy | Land Use & Agriculture
Scope_And_Commitments: Government's plan to achieve clean power (>95% zero-carbon electricity) in Great Britain by 2030. Targets: 50 GW offshore wind, 27–29 GW onshore wind, 45–47 GW solar by 2030. Sets out planning reform, grid connections reform, accelerated consenting for renewable energy. Led jointly by DESNZ and NESO.
Intl_Links: [EU-L-019] EU Renewable Energy Directive III (Directive EU 2023/2413 — RED III recast)

Name: Industrial Decarbonisation Strategy 2021
Policy_Sector: Climate | Energy
Scope_And_Commitments: Strategy for decarbonising UK industry by ~71% by 2035. Covers CCUS deployment (HyNet, East Coast Cluster), hydrogen for industry, energy efficiency, fuel switching. Sets out cluster sequencing programme.

Name: Jet Zero Strategy 2022
Policy_Sector: Climate | Energy | Transport
Scope_And_Commitments: UK's strategy for net-zero aviation by 2050. SAF mandate from 2025 (2% blend), rising to 10% by 2030. R&D for zero-emission flight. Demand management principles. Published by DfT.

Name: UK Hydrogen Strategy 2021
Policy_Sector: Climate | Energy
Scope_And_Commitments: Strategy to develop 10 GW of low-carbon hydrogen production by 2030. Covers electrolytic and CCUS-enabled hydrogen. Hydrogen business models, Net Zero Hydrogen Fund, village heating trials. Hydrogen levy (in Energy Act 2023).

Name: Land Use Framework (LUF) 2025
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Energy | Land Use & Agriculture
Scope_And_Commitments: Sets principles for multifunctional land use in England — balancing food production, nature recovery, net-zero, housing. Five land use principles proposed in January 2025 consultation. Will align housing, infrastructure, energy and nature targets spatially. NISTA to coordinate cross-government spatial planning. [Themes: nature-based solutions; natural capital; ecosystem services]

Name: England Peat Action Plan 2021
Policy_Sector: Climate | Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture
Scope_And_Commitments: Plan to restore and rewet damaged peatland. Target: 280,000 ha restored by 2050; >5,000 ha/year restored by 2025. Bans burning of peat on protected sites. Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture

Name: Boiler Upgrade Scheme (BUS)
Policy_Sector: Climate | Energy
Scope_And_Commitments: Grants of £7,500 for heat pump installations (air source and ground source) and £5,000 for biomass boilers in off-gas-grid homes. Supports 600,000 heat pump installations/year by 2028 target. Funded from DESNZ budget.

Name: Contracts for Difference (CfD) scheme
Policy_Sector: Climate | Energy
Scope_And_Commitments: Main support mechanism for large-scale renewable electricity (offshore/onshore wind, solar, tidal, nuclear). Government auctions long-term strike prices guaranteeing revenue for generators. AR4 secured 11 GW. AR6 ongoing. Delivered by Low Carbon Contracts Company (LCCC) under DESNZ.
Intl_Links: [EU-L-019] EU Renewable Energy Directive III (Directive EU 2023/2413 — RED III recast)

Name: Climate Change Risk Assessment (CCRA3) 2022
Policy_Sector: Climate
Scope_And_Commitments:
Third statutory CCRA covering 61 UK climate risks/opportunities across 5 themes. Forms basis for NAP3. CCRA4 will commence 2026–27 ahead of NAP4. Produced by CCC with government support.

[VERSION HISTORY] CCRA3 (2022) is the third statutory assessment under CCA 2008 s.56. Previous versions: CCRA1 (2012), CCRA2 (2017). Covers 61 UK climate risks/opportunities across 5 themes. Forms basis for NAP3. CCRA4 will commence 2026–27 ahead of NAP4. Produced by CCC with government support. CCRA3 found adaptation progress 'insufficient' across most risk areas.

[CURRENCY] The Fourth Independent Assessment of UK Climate Risk (CCRA4-IA) was published by the CCC on 20 May 2026 as "A Well-Adapted UK", with a Technical Report led by the Met Office. Brings together public sector organisations (including EA, JNCC, Natural England, UKCEH, Met Office, Cefas, BGS, NOC) to maximise value and minimise duplication of environmental monitoring. Name: UK Marine Strategy (UKMS) 2025 — Programme of Measures
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Marine & Fisheries | Water

Lead_Organisation: [ORG-001] Defra & [ORG-034] Scottish Govt & [ORG-035] Welsh Govt & [ORG-036] NI Executive (DAERA)
Scope_And_Commitments: Statutory 3-part strategy required by Marine Strategy Regulations. Covers UK seas (English, Welsh, Scottish and NI waters). Name: Woodland Carbon Code (WCC)
Policy_Sector: Climate | Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture
Scope_And_Commitments: UK voluntary standard for woodland carbon credits. Developed and maintained by Scottish Forestry, Forestry Commission England and NRW. Projects must demonstrate additionality, permanence (100 years) and scientific rigour. Generates Pending Issuance Units (PIUs) and Woodland Carbon Units (WCUs) verified against the Code. Widely used by businesses and landowners to fund new woodland creation — linked to ELM Landscape Recovery scheme and contributes to England's woodland creation targets. Part of UK's voluntary nature market infrastructure alongside the Peatland Code. [Themes: nature-based solutions; natural capital; ecosystem services]

Name: Peatland Code
Policy_Sector: Climate | Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture | Governance, Society & Data
Scope_And_Commitments: UK voluntary certification standard for peatland restoration carbon projects. Managed by the IUCN Peatlands Programme (hosted by the University of Exeter) with support from Natural England. Projects certified against Code generate Peatland Carbon Units (PCUs) — internationally recognised Voluntary Carbon Market credits. Demonstrates additionality, permanence and GHG benefits of peatland rewetting. Directly supports Nature for Climate Fund peat restoration targets (280,000 ha restored by 2050). Enables private finance to fund peatland restoration with rigorous scientific standards. [Themes: nature-based solutions; natural capital; ecosystem services]
Intl_Links: [INT-O-017] International Union for Conservation of Nature

Name: Nutrient Neutrality Scheme
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Water | Land Use & Agriculture
Scope_And_Commitments: Natural England-administered mechanism requiring new residential development in Habitats Regulations-sensitive river catchments (currently ~74 local authority areas) to demonstrate nutrient neutrality before planning permission is granted. Developers must offset nitrogen or phosphorus pollution through land management agreements (e.g., converting arable to grassland, wetland creation) or purchase of nutrient credits from Natural England's Nutrient Mitigation Scheme. Directly links habitat creation and restoration (lowland meadows, wetlands) to planning permissions. Links nature recovery with housebuilding. NAO reviewed in 2024; Planning and Infrastructure Bill proposes reform via Environmental Delivery Plans. [Themes: nature-based solutions; natural capital; ecosystem services]

Name: Tree Health Resilience Strategy 2018
Policy_Sector: Climate | Marine & Fisheries | Land Use & Agriculture | Biosecurity
Year_Status: 2018 (remains current; now implemented through Plant Biosecurity Strategy 2023–28)
Scope_And_Commitments: Defra/Forestry Commission strategy to protect England's tree population from pest and disease threats (including Ash Dieback, Oak Processionary Moth, Xylella). Contains a National Action Plan. Sets risk-based biosecurity approach, goals for tree resilience (extent, connectivity, diversity, condition), and actions for inspection, surveillance and citizen reporting (Observatree). Directly relevant to tree and woodland targets in Environment Act 2021 and England Trees Action Plan (woodland cover, woodland carbon). Implemented by Forestry Commission and APHA jointly.
Intl_Links: [INT-L-023] International Plant Protection Convention

Name: Plant Biosecurity Strategy for Great Britain (2023–2028)
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Marine & Fisheries | Land Use & Agriculture | Biosecurity
Lead_Organisation: [ORG-001] Defra & [ORG-034] Scottish Govt & [ORG-035] Welsh Govt | [ORG-020] APHA & [ORG-009] FC & [ORG-028] Scottish Forestry & [ORG-015] NRW
Scope_And_Commitments: Cross-government GB strategy for biosecurity of plants (including trees) and plant products. Addresses risks from internationally traded plant material (18.6 million tonnes imported to UK annually). Sets goals for prevention, preparedness, response and recovery from plant pest and disease incursions. Covers: import controls, surveillance networks (including Observatree citizen science), emergency response plans, international collaboration, research and capabilities. Directly relevant to INNS targets (GBF Target 6, JNCC B6) and woodland/habitat condition targets under Environment Act 2021. Implemented by APHA, Forestry Commission, Scottish Forestry, NRW, Welsh Government.
Intl_Links: [INT-L-023] International Plant Protection Convention; [INT-O-028] European and Mediterranean Plant Protection Organization; [INT-P-004] IPBES Invasive Alien Species Assessment 2023

Name: Climate & Environment Cross-Government Working Group
Policy_Sector: Climate | Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture
Scope_And_Commitments: Internal cross-departmental working group coordinating climate and environment policy across Whitehall departments. Ensures coherence between climate mitigation, adaptation and nature policies in the development of the CBDP, NAP, EIP and related plans. Brings together senior officials from DESNZ, Defra, HM Treasury, MHCLG, DfT, Cabinet Office and other departments. Not publicly visible — operates within normal government inter-departmental coordination processes. Referenced in Notion document as a key UK governance mechanism.

Name: NAP Biodiversity and Ecosystems Working Group (NAP-BEWG)
Policy_Sector: Climate | Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture
Scope_And_Commitments: Advisory working group providing expert input to the biodiversity and ecosystems theme of the National Adaptation Programme (NAP3, 2023–2028). Advises Defra on how to protect and enhance biodiversity and ecosystem services in the context of climate change adaptation. Brings together experts from Natural England, JNCC, Environment Agency, academic institutions and NGOs. Feeds into the 'Biodiversity and Ecosystems' chapter of the NAP and informs Defra's reporting to the CCC on adaptation progress. Directly relevant to the climate–nature interface — its work links climate projections with biodiversity and ecosystem service delivery.

Name: Environmental Delivery Plans (EDPs)
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Water | Pollution & Waste | Land Use & Agriculture
Year_Status: 2025 (framework in force; first EDPs in preparation)
Related_Policy_Links: [POL-038] Nature Restoration Fund and Nature Restoration Levy (NRF / NRL)
Scope_And_Commitments: Strategic conservation plans, prepared by Natural England, that identify environmental impacts of development on protected sites or species and set out conservation measures to address them. Developers may discharge specified obligations by paying the Nature Restoration Levy into the Nature Restoration Fund [POL-038] instead of providing project-level mitigation; full Habitats Regulations appropriate assessment still applies where impacts fall outside an EDP. [Themes: nature-based solutions; natural capital; ecosystem services]

Name: Nature Restoration Fund and Nature Restoration Levy (NRF / NRL)
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Water | Finance | Land Use & Agriculture
Scope_And_Commitments: Pooled fund, administered by Natural England, financed by a Nature Restoration Levy paid by developers who opt into an Environmental Delivery Plan [POL-037]. Funds strategic, at-scale conservation and habitat-restoration measures (including river pollution reduction) as an alternative to project-level mitigation. Widely debated for nature outcomes; secondary legislation to follow. [Themes: nature-based solutions; natural capital; ecosystem services]

Name: Independent Water Commission (Cunliffe Review) — Final Report
Policy_Sector: Water | Nature & Biodiversity | Governance, Society & Data
Year_Status: 2025 (final report 21 Jul 2025; government response and reforms under way)
Scope_And_Commitments: Root-and-branch review of water-sector regulation in England and Wales, making 88 recommendations. Government has accepted the headline recommendation to abolish Ofwat and create a single water regulator, merging Ofwat with the water functions of the Environment Agency, Natural England and the Drinking Water Inspectorate. Bears directly on the regulatory architecture for water quality, abstraction and catchment management.

Name: Nature for Climate Fund

Funds the England Trees Action Plan [POL-011] and England Peat Action Plan [POL-010] and supports the Woodland Carbon Code [POL-030] and Peatland Code [POL-031]. [Themes: nature-based solutions; natural capital; ecosystem services]

Name: Enabling a Natural Capital Approach (ENCA)

Scope_And_Commitments: Defra guidance, data and tools for incorporating natural capital and ecosystem services into policy, programme and project appraisal. Operational backbone of natural-capital accounting and valuation in government decision-making; complements the Green Book guidance [POL-042] and the NCEA programme [POL-026]. [Themes: nature-based solutions; natural capital; ecosystem services]

Name: Green Book supplementary guidance: environmental and natural capital valuation

Year_Status: Ongoing (supplementary guidance to the HMT Green Book)
Scope_And_Commitments: HM Treasury Green Book supplementary guidance on valuing environmental impacts, greenhouse gas emissions (carbon values) and natural capital in appraisal and evaluation. Sets the methodology by which climate and nature effects enter government cost-benefit analysis. [Themes: nature-based solutions; natural capital; ecosystem services]

Name: The Economics of Biodiversity: The Dasgupta Review
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Finance
Related_Policy_Links: [POL-012] Green Finance Strategy 2023; [POL-041] Enabling a Natural Capital Approach (ENCA)
Scope_And_Commitments: Independent, HM Treasury-commissioned review framing biodiversity as an economic asset and the economy as embedded within nature. Foundational reference for the UK natural-capital and green-finance agenda; shaped the Green Finance Strategy [POL-012] and natural-capital approach [POL-041]. [Themes: nature-based solutions; natural capital; ecosystem services]

Name: UK National Ecosystem Assessment (UK NEA)
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Governance, Society & Data
Related_Policy_Links: [POL-026] Natural Capital and Ecosystem Assessment (NCEA) Programme
Scope_And_Commitments: First comprehensive assessment of the UK natural environment in terms of ecosystem services and the benefits they provide to society. Foundational evidence for the ecosystem-services and natural-capital agenda and lineage of the later Natural Capital and Ecosystem Assessment programme [POL-026]. [Themes: nature-based solutions; natural capital; ecosystem services]

Name: National Flood and Coastal Erosion Risk Management Strategy for England
Policy_Sector: Water | Climate | Land Use & Agriculture | Nature & Biodiversity
Related_Policy_Links: [POL-002] National Adaptation Programme (NAP3) 2023–2028; [POL-017] Climate Change Risk Assessment (CCRA3) 2022; [POL-070] NaFRA2 national flood and coastal erosion risk assessment
Scope_And_Commitments: Environment Agency statutory strategy setting long-term ambitions for a nation resilient to flooding and coastal change to 2100, with an accompanying action plan. Increasingly emphasises nature-based and catchment-scale solutions and adaptation; aligns with NAP3 [POL-002] and CCRA3 [POL-017]. [Themes: nature-based solutions; natural capital; ecosystem services]

Name: Transport Decarbonisation Plan (Decarbonising Transport)
Policy_Sector: Climate | Energy | Transport
Related_Policy_Links: [POL-004] UK Net Zero Strategy / Carbon Budget Delivery Plan (CBDP) 2023
Scope_And_Commitments: Cross-modal strategy for decarbonising surface transport (the largest-emitting UK sector), aviation and maritime, with commitments spanning road vehicle phase-out, modal shift and zero-emission technologies. Sectoral counterpart to the Net Zero Strategy / Carbon Budget Delivery Plan [POL-004].

Name: Heat and Buildings Strategy
Policy_Sector: Climate | Energy
Scope_And_Commitments: Strategy for decarbonising heat in buildings, covering heat pumps, hydrogen for heat options, energy efficiency and market mechanisms. Strategic parent of delivery schemes such as the Boiler Upgrade Scheme [POL-015].

Name: Biomass Strategy 2023
Policy_Sector: Climate | Energy | Land Use & Agriculture
Scope_And_Commitments: Cross-government strategy on the role of sustainable biomass across the economy, including priority use, sustainability criteria and bioenergy with carbon capture and storage (BECCS). Interfaces with land use, forestry and nature through feedstock and land-use trade-offs.

Name: Marine Climate Change Impacts Partnership (MCCIP)
Policy_Sector: Climate | Nature & Biodiversity | Marine & Fisheries
Year_Status: Ongoing (launched 2005); Phase V business plan 2025-2030; rolling evidence updates
Lead_Organisation: [ORG-018] Cefas (hosts secretariat); Defra-chaired steering group of UK govts, agencies & NGOs
Scope_And_Commitments: UK partnership of scientists, government, agencies and NGOs providing co-ordinated, quality-assured evidence on marine climate change impacts and adaptation. Originated from the 2005 Charting Progress assessment of UK seas. Delivers a rolling evidence programme (formerly biennial report cards 2006-2020) covering sea temperature, ocean acidification, ocean circulation, shelf-sea stratification, oxygen, sea-level rise, storms/waves, Arctic sea ice, fish, fisheries, marine mammals and seabirds, plus marine-heatwave policy briefs. Recent updates: Sea Temperature (Oct 2025), Ocean Circulation (Sep 2025), Oxygen (Aug 2025), Ocean Acidification (Feb 2025). Met Office is a partner and leads the Arctic Sea Ice topic. Primary supplier of marine climate evidence into UK adaptation governance (CCRA, NAP) and the UK Marine Strategy [POL-028].
Extent: UK (with separate report cards for Crown Dependencies & Overseas Territories)
Intl_Links: [INT-O-027] Arctic Monitoring and Assessment Programme; [INT-P-032] IPCC Special Report on the Ocean and Cryosphere in a Changing Climate (SROCC) 2019; [INT-P-033] UN Decade of Ocean Science for Sustainable Development (2021-2030)

Name: National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF)
Policy_Sector: Urban & Buildings | Land Use & Agriculture | Nature & Biodiversity | Climate | Energy
Year_Status: Dec 2024 (revised; amended Feb 2025; further reforms consulted Dec 2025)
Related_Policy_Links: [POL-009] Land Use Framework (LUF) 2025
Scope_And_Commitments: Sets out the government's planning policies for England and how they are applied in plan-making and decision-taking. The operative instrument mediating development against climate, nature and land-use objectives: mandatory housing targets (1.5m homes), 'grey belt' release, brownfield-first, reversal of the onshore-wind ban, biodiversity net gain, flood-risk and renewable-energy policy. Sits above local plans and complements the Land Use Framework [POL-009]. Further reform package consulted Dec 2025. [Themes: spatial planning; land-use change; development control]

Name: Towards a Good Food Cycle (UK Government Food Strategy framework)
Policy_Sector: Land Use & Agriculture | Climate | Nature & Biodiversity | Governance, Society & Data
Scope_And_Commitments: Defra framework (15 July 2025) setting ten priority outcomes for the England food system across health, food security, economic growth and environmental impact. Targets diet-related emissions, greener supply chains and supply-chain resilience. Notes agriculture at ~11.7% of UK GHG emissions, projected to be a dominant emission source (with aviation) by 2040. Successor framing to the 2021 Dimbleby National Food Strategy; binding delivery measures to follow. [Themes: food systems; agricultural emissions; food security]

Name: UK Pesticides National Action Plan 2025
Policy_Sector: Land Use & Agriculture | Nature & Biodiversity | Water | Biosecurity
Lead_Organisation: [ORG-001] Defra & [ORG-034] Scottish Govt & [ORG-035] Welsh Govt & [ORG-036] NI Executive (DAERA)
Scope_And_Commitments: First UK pesticides NAP in a decade (21 March 2025), agreed by all four governments. Sets the UK's first domestic pesticide reduction target — a 10% cut in potential environmental harm by 2030 (harm-based, not volume-based) — structured around three objectives: uptake of integrated pest management (IPM); reduction timetables and targets; and strengthened compliance. Supports pollinators (follows the ban on three neonicotinoids in England) and links pesticide use to climate, invasive species and food security. Directly relevant to the Met Office plant pest/pathogen biosecurity strand. [Themes: agri-environment; pollinators; integrated pest management]

Name: Nature Markets Framework 2023
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Finance | Land Use & Agriculture | Climate
Related_Policy_Links: [POL-038] Nature Restoration Fund and Nature Restoration Levy (NRF / NRL)
Scope_And_Commitments: Government framework (March 2023) to scale private investment in nature recovery and sustainable farming towards a target of £1bn/year private finance into nature in England by 2030 (£500m by 2027). Provides the overarching architecture above the component instruments already catalogued — Woodland Carbon Code [POL-030], Peatland Code [POL-031], Biodiversity Net Gain units [LEG-008] and the Nature Restoration Fund [POL-038] — with measures on high-integrity standards, market governance and the British Standards Institution nature investment standards programme. [Themes: nature markets; natural capital; green finance]

Name: Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI)
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture | Climate
Scope_And_Commitments: The universal, entry-level tier of the ELM schemes paying farmers for actions on soil health, hedgerows, integrated pest management, nutrient management, cover crops and habitat. SFI 2023 and the SFI 2024 expanded/re-opened offers are closed to new applications (window closed 11 March 2025 on budget exhaustion; ~37,000 agreements live; re-opened briefly for in-flight applicants to Aug 2025). A reformed 'SFI26' offer with confirmed funding and revised actions is expected in the first half of 2026. Distinct from the broader ELM umbrella [POL-013] and Countryside Stewardship Higher Tier / Landscape Recovery. [Themes: agri-environment; public money for public goods; soil health]

Name: England Woodland Creation Offer (EWCO)
Policy_Sector: Climate | Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture | Water
Year_Status: 2021 – ongoing (funding confirmed to Mar 2027; phased transition into ELM)
Related_Policy_Links: [POL-013] Environmental Land Management (ELM) Schemes; [POL-030] Woodland Carbon Code (WCC); [POL-011] England Trees Action Plan 2021–2024
Scope_And_Commitments: National woodland-creation grant administered by the Forestry Commission for areas as small as 1 ha. Up to £10,200/ha standard capital costs, up to ~£11,600–£12,700/ha stackable payments for wider public benefits (nature recovery, water quality, flood risk, climate, access), plus £400/ha/year maintenance for 15 years. Funded via the Nature for Climate Fund [POL-040]; funding confirmed to 31 March 2027 with a phased transition into the ELM schemes [POL-013]. Refreshed guidance Oct 2025. Stacks with the Woodland Carbon Code [POL-030] and supports the England Trees Action Plan [POL-011]. [Themes: afforestation; carbon sequestration; nature-based solutions]

Name: Sustainable Farming Scheme (Wales)
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture | Climate
Related_Policy_Links: [POL-013] Environmental Land Management (ELM) Schemes
Scope_And_Commitments: Wales' primary post-CAP land-management support scheme, launching 1 January 2026 (transition period to 2029), replacing the Basic Payment Scheme. Three-layer design: a Universal Layer (Universal Actions + baseline payment, incl. habitat maintenance, soil/water and the 10% tree-cover and 10% habitat ambitions), plus Optional and Collaborative Actions for targeted climate, nature and water outcomes. Anchored in the Sustainable Land Management objectives of the Agriculture (Wales) Act 2023. Devolved counterpart to England's ELM [POL-013]. [Themes: agri-environment; sustainable land management; devolved agriculture]

Name: Agricultural Reform Programme (Scotland)
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture | Climate
Year_Status: Act 2024; provisions commenced Jun 2025; full framework by 2027
Related_Policy_Links: [POL-013] Environmental Land Management (ELM) Schemes; [POL-056] Sustainable Farming Scheme (Wales)
Scope_And_Commitments: Scotland's framework for future agricultural support replacing CAP-era payments, enabled by the Agriculture and Rural Communities (Scotland) Act 2024 (key provisions commenced 16 June 2025). Delivered via the Agricultural Reform Route Map and the National Test Programme, with a four-tier future support structure (base/enhanced/elective/complementary) conditioned on climate and nature outcomes. Transitional period 2025–2026; full implementation expected 2027. Devolved counterpart to England's ELM [POL-013] and the Wales SFS [POL-056]. [Themes: agri-environment; conditionality; devolved agriculture]

Name: Clean Air Strategy 2019
Policy_Sector: Pollution & Waste | Nature & Biodiversity | Climate | Land Use & Agriculture
Year_Status: 2019 – ongoing (PM2.5 targets set under Environment Act 2021, 2023)
Related_Policy_Links: [POL-001] Environmental Improvement Plan (EIP) 2025
Scope_And_Commitments: Cross-government strategy (Jan 2019) to cut emissions of the five priority air pollutants, including the first national action on agricultural ammonia (~88% of UK ammonia from farming) via controls on fertiliser use and slurry management. Addresses links between air quality, ecosystem damage (nitrogen deposition on sensitive habitats) and climate. Now operationalised through the Environment Act 2021 statutory PM2.5 targets (2023) and the Environmental Improvement Plan [POL-001]. [Themes: air quality; ammonia; nitrogen deposition]

Name: UK Marine Policy Statement (MPS) and Marine Plans
Policy_Sector: Marine & Fisheries | Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture | Energy | Climate
Year_Status: 2011 (MPS); Marine Plans rolling to 2021; in implementation
Related_Policy_Links: [POL-009] Land Use Framework (LUF) 2025; [POL-050] National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF); [POL-028] UK Marine Strategy (UKMS) 2025 — Programme of Measures
Scope_And_Commitments: The shared UK framework (adopted 2011 by the four administrations) for sustainable development of the marine area, implemented through marine plans that allocate space for fishing, aquaculture, offshore renewables, cabling, conservation and recreation. In England, MMO-prepared marine plans now cover all English waters. The marine-space counterpart to the terrestrial Land Use Framework [POL-009] and NPPF [POL-050]; decision-makers must act in accordance with the MPS and plans. Distinct from the UK Marine Strategy [POL-028], which sets environmental status objectives rather than spatial allocation. [Themes: marine spatial planning; sea-use; blue economy]

Name: Highly Protected Marine Areas (HPMAs)
Policy_Sector: Marine & Fisheries | Nature & Biodiversity | Climate
Year_Status: First 3 designated Jun 2023; network expansion under development
Related_Policy_Links: [POL-022] 30×30 Technical Working Group
Scope_And_Commitments: Areas of English sea given the highest protection — prohibiting extractive, destructive and depositional activities to allow full ecosystem (and 'blue carbon') recovery. First three pilot HPMAs designated June 2023 (Allonby Bay, Dolphin Head, North East of Farnes Deep) following the 2020 Benyon Review. Network expansion under development: a plan for further designations and the Environmental Audit Committee's call for 10% of UK waters as HPMAs by 2030 (linked to the 30x30 target, [POL-022]). Sit within the wider MPA network (181 MPAs, ~40% of English waters). [Themes: marine protected areas; whole-site protection; blue carbon]

Name: Countryside Stewardship Higher Tier (CSHT)
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture | Climate | Water
Related_Policy_Links: [POL-054] Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI); [POL-062] Landscape Recovery
Scope_And_Commitments: One of the three Environmental Land Management (ELM) scheme components (with SFI, [POL-054], and Landscape Recovery, [POL-062]). Pays farmers and land managers for targeted, often bespoke actions to protect, restore and enhance the environment and mitigate climate change, on farmed land, woodland and land managed for nature. Replaces the former CS Higher Tier and Higher Level Stewardship (HLS). Opened to invited applicants from 15 September 2025 via the Rural Payments Agency (RPA), with pre-application advice from Natural England and the Forestry Commission; rolling monthly application windows. 2025 offer: 99 base actions, 33 supplements, 142 capital items; agreements of 5-20 years. 2026/27 budget GBP 50m.

Name: Landscape Recovery
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture | Climate | Water
Scope_And_Commitments: The most ambitious of the three ELM scheme components (with SFI, [POL-054], and Countryside Stewardship Higher Tier, [POL-061]). Funds large-scale, long-term (typically 500-5,000 ha, 20+ year) bespoke habitat and ecosystem-restoration projects co-designed with farmers and land managers, blending public and private finance. Round 1 (2022): 22 pilot projects; Round 2 (2023): 34 projects, GBP 25m, >700 farmers across ~200,000 ha. First two projects entered implementation August 2025 (GBP 55m blended finance). Round 3 expected during 2026. Agreements entered with Natural England and the Environment Agency.

Name: Catchment Sensitive Farming (CSF)
Policy_Sector: Water | Land Use & Agriculture | Pollution & Waste | Nature & Biodiversity
Scope_And_Commitments: Long-running partnership between Natural England, the Environment Agency and Defra (delivered by Natural England advisers) providing free one-to-one advice, training and capital-grant support to farmers to reduce diffuse water and air pollution and improve soil health. Expanded to cover 100% of England farmland by 2023 (annual budget ~GBP 30m). Supports Countryside Stewardship / ELM capital-grant applications, natural flood management and Water Framework Directive objectives.

Name: Farming in Protected Landscapes (FiPL)
Policy_Sector: Land Use & Agriculture | Nature & Biodiversity | Climate
Scope_And_Commitments: Defra-funded competitive grant programme, developed with and delivered locally by National Park and National Landscape teams, supporting farmers and land managers in England National Parks, National Landscapes (formerly AONBs) and the Broads to deliver projects for climate, nature, people and place. Part of the Agricultural Transition Plan; explicitly not an agri-environment scheme. Began July 2021; extended to 31 March 2029 (confirmed January 2026); GBP 30m for 2026/27, >GBP 130m committed since launch. Contributes to the Protected Landscapes Targets and Outcomes Framework and 30by30.

Name: Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG)
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture
Scope_And_Commitments: Statutory requirement that most new development in England deliver a measurable 10% increase in biodiversity value, calculated with the statutory biodiversity metric (produced by Defra and Natural England) and secured for at least 30 years via planning condition, s.106 agreement or conservation covenant. Met through on-site gains, registered off-site gains or statutory biodiversity credits (sold by Natural England). Mandatory for major development from 12 February 2024, small sites from 2 April 2024, and Nationally Significant Infrastructure Projects from May 2026. MHCLG leads associated planning policy.

Name: Peatland ACTION (Scotland)
Policy_Sector: Climate | Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture | Water
Related_Policy_Links: [POL-010] England Peat Action Plan 2021
Scope_And_Commitments: Scotland national peatland restoration programme, led and funded by the Scottish Government and delivered by a five-partner partnership (NatureScot as lead, Forestry and Land Scotland, Cairngorms National Park Authority, Loch Lomond & the Trossachs National Park Authority, Scottish Water). Running since 2012; GBP 250m committed over 10 years to 2030 toward a target of 250,000 ha restored by 2030 (>90,000 ha to date). Funds up to 100% of restoration costs plus advice, training and monitoring; many projects also use the IUCN Peatland Code. A five-year Partnership Plan 2025-2030 sets delivery strategy. England equivalent: England Peat Action Plan [POL-010].

Name: Fisheries Act 2020 climate change objective — Joint Fisheries Statement (JFS) and Fisheries Management Plans (FMPs)
Policy_Sector: Marine & Fisheries | Climate | Nature & Biodiversity
Year_Status: Act 2020; JFS Nov 2022; FMPs rolling from 2023 (ongoing)
Lead_Organisation: [ORG-001] Defra & [ORG-008] MMO & [ORG-034] Scottish Govt & [ORG-035] Welsh Govt & [ORG-036] NI Executive (DAERA)
Scope_And_Commitments: Statutory UK fisheries framework under the Fisheries Act 2020. The eight fisheries objectives include a climate change objective — minimising the adverse effects of fish and aquaculture activities on climate change and adapting fisheries management to it. The Joint Fisheries Statement (JFS, Nov 2022) sets the overarching direction and commits the four fisheries policy authorities to an ecosystem-based approach; Fisheries Management Plans (FMPs) set stock- and area-specific goals and actions, and are recognised measures in the 2025 UK Marine Strategy Programme of Measures. Climate-driven shifts in the distribution, productivity and phenology of stocks are a central management challenge that ocean-temperature and marine-heatwave evidence could inform.

Name: Shellfish official-control and harmful algal bloom (HAB) / biotoxin monitoring (Cefas for FSA / Food Standards Scotland)
Policy_Sector: Marine & Fisheries | Biosecurity
Year_Status: Ongoing (statutory official controls; results published weekly)
Scope_And_Commitments: Official-control monitoring of classified shellfish harvesting areas — microbiological (E. coli) classification, and biotoxin and phytoplankton (harmful algal bloom) monitoring — delivered by Cefas on behalf of the Food Standards Agency (England, Wales, Northern Ireland) and Food Standards Scotland, with results published weekly and final classification set by the FSA/FSS. Marine heatwaves are linked to increased harmful algal blooms and elevated pathogenic Vibrio in UK shellfish waters (e.g. the 2018 event); ocean-temperature and marine-heatwave forecasts could give early warning to target biotoxin and Vibrio risk, protecting shellfisheries and public health.

Name: UK Blue Carbon Evidence Partnership (UKBCEP)
Policy_Sector: Climate | Nature & Biodiversity | Marine & Fisheries
Lead_Organisation: [ORG-001] Defra & [ORG-018] Cefas & [ORG-002] DESNZ & [ORG-034] Scottish Govt & [ORG-035] Welsh Govt & [ORG-036] NI Executive (DAERA)
Scope_And_Commitments: Cross-administration partnership coordinating the UK blue-carbon evidence base (saltmarsh, seagrass, kelp and seabed sediments), including a working group on the inclusion of saltmarsh and seagrass in the UK Greenhouse Gas Inventory. Marine heatwaves damage seagrass and saltmarsh and can alter coastal-carbon storage and flux, so ocean-temperature and marine-heatwave evidence is relevant to blue-carbon condition and permanence assessment.

Name: National assessment of flood and coastal erosion risk in England (NaFRA2)
Policy_Sector: Water | Urban & Buildings | Climate
Related_Policy_Links: [POL-045] National FCERM Strategy for England
Scope_And_Commitments:
The Environment Agency’s national picture of current and future flood and coastal erosion risk in England: the sources and characteristics of risk, its distribution across England, and how it is expected to change. The 2024 assessment reports a changed picture of risk arising from a combination of updated climate change projections, improved understanding and assessment of risk, and better modelling and new data. The EA states that risk is not static and that the assessment will be updated regularly.

[INDICATOR LINK] NaFRA is the underlying risk assessment behind [IND-E-042], the EIF Theme F indicator "Disruption or unwanted impacts from flooding or coastal erosion", which already names it as a data source. This record gives the assessment itself a place in the governance workbook; the indicator remains the measure.

Name: Monitoring the condition of the natural environment (Environment Act 2021 s.16 statement)
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Governance, Society & Data
Related_Policy_Links: [POL-001] Environmental Improvement Plan
Scope_And_Commitments:
The statutory statement laid before Parliament under section 16 of the Environment Act 2021, setting out the kinds of data that will be obtained to monitor whether the natural environment, or a particular aspect of it, is improving. It covers progress towards the 13 Environment Act 2021 targets and their interim targets, in accordance with the Environmental Improvement Plan.

[SCOPE NOTE] This is the monitoring architecture behind [IFW-01], the Environmental Indicator Framework: it describes what data Defra will obtain, where the EIF is the indicator set reported from it. Earlier versions are in the UK Government Web Archive. NOTE ON DATE: the queue recorded this as a July 2026 publication; 16 July 2026 is the latest update to a statement first published in May 2022.
